prerequisites: Elasticity and Strength of Materials II

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of the engineering disciplines specific to their specialty, at the level necessary to acquire the rest of the degree competencies, including notions of the latest advances.
Awareness of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.

Ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; choose and apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods appropriately and correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

Ability to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems in their specialty; appropriately choose and apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods; recognize the importance of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial constraints.

Ability to perform bibliographic searches, consult and critically use databases and other information sources, to carry out simulation and analysis with the aim of conducting research on technical topics in their specialty.
Ability to consult and apply good practice and safety codes in their specialty.
Capacity and skill to design and conduct experimental investigations, interpret results, and draw conclusions in their field of study.
Understanding of applicable techniques and methods of analysis, design, and research and their limitations in their specialty.
Practical competence to solve complex problems, carry out complex engineering projects, and conduct research specific to their specialty.
Knowledge of the application of materials, equipment and tools, technology, and engineering processes and their limitations in their specialty.
Ability to apply engineering practice standards in their specialty.
Ability to collect and interpret data and manage complex concepts within their specialty, to make judgments that involve reflection on ethical and social issues.
Ability to manage complex technical or professional activities or projects in their specialty, taking responsibility for decision-making.
Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions in the field of engineering and to society in general.
Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and to cooperate with both engineers and people from other disciplines.
Ability to stay updated on new developments in science and technology.
Use measurement systems for monitoring industrial production processes.

syllabus_topics: Theory on measurement chain, acquisition and signal processing.
Execution of laboratory practices: experimental results processing using MATLAB.
Execution of laboratory practices: construction of applications for experimental data acquisition and processing using LABVIEW.
teaching_methods: Project work (individual or team), report writing and presentation
Problem-solving practices in real and/or simulated contexts

assessment_methods.method: Project evaluation (technical capacity, project involvement, work performed, results, documentation, technical presentation and defense), including submission of report and Matlab/Labview programs.
Individual written test for technical competencies.
Project evaluation (technical capacity, project involvement, work performed, results, documentation, technical presentation and defense), including submission of report and Matlab programs.

assessment_rules: For RGM425 and RGM424: evaluation consists of submitting a report and programs (Matlab or Labview), and their correction. Participation and technical competence shown in class will also be evaluated. The maximum grade after recovery is 5.0. For RGM423: an individual written test is required with a minimum grade of 4.0. If the minimum is not reached, a recovery test is mandatory, with the final grade calculated as 25% of the initial test and 75% of the recovery test.
